acceptance: Only the PuppyOne host family over HTTPS, or localhost development, is ever a Cloud endpoint: empty, blank, non-HTTP and unparsable values, an insecure production endpoint (never upgraded), other hosts, link-local metadata and private addresses, and a lookalike parent domain are refused. A trailing slash names the same endpoint and another host does not. There is no implicit endpoint: without an explicit packaged or development configuration Cloud is not configured.

reason: TS normalizes whatever endpoint it is given: it strips a query and fragment, accepts a bare production origin as the API base and prefixes a relative API path with '/'. The native app validates its one configured Environment instead of repairing it: the API base must end in /api/v1, a query, fragment or credentials refuse the configuration, and Environment::api_url refuses any path that is not absolute (all callers use fixed absolute paths). Insecure endpoints are refused, never upgraded, in both.

TS derives an API base from a repository's PuppyOne remote (cloudApiBaseUrlFromRemote) and, unless the configured API is loopback, sends that repository's requests there. The native app never takes an endpoint from a remote: a remote can only name a Project on the configured origin (or the explicit loopback hosted-Git mapping), so a repository cannot redirect requests or credentials to another Cloud.

acceptance: A repository-context resolution that cannot reach Cloud, times out or is cancelled is reported as such after one send, never retried. Through the real HTTP adapter a refusal keeps the server's allowlisted code, its retry decision and a plain request id; an id that is not a plain token and an unlisted code are dropped; a 409's safe data.code (initialization_not_abandonable) is kept rather than classified with every 409; an unreachable Cloud is unavailable; and a reply whose body stalls after its headers times out like one that never answers.

reason: These check how Electron's Main process composes its network stack: Chromium's net.fetch instead of Node's fetch (with credentials 'omit' and bypassCustomProtocolHandlers), a transport that must be injected, a DataPort's session guard not mistaken for a fetch transport, an opt-in bytes response no TS caller asks for, and an HTTP status written into the error message so it survives IPC serialization. The native app has one in-process reqwest client (no cookie store; redirects refused, see transport_rejects_redirects_and_privileged_or_oversized_configurations), JSON replies only, and typed errors that keep their status without crossing an IPC boundary; server prose is never shown.
